transcript.answer: Otto picks the persona with `selectPersona(registry, message)`. That function is pure, has no I/O and no classifier call, and is deterministic. It takes only the registry and the text of the latest customer message. It must not take the session, a user id or a customer number, so who the customer is never influences the choice. Selection is a case-insensitive substring match of the message against each persona's `match` keyword list. When several personas match equally, the first one declared wins. Otherwise it falls back to the default persona. That fallback applies to an empty message, a message over 10,000 characters, a missing `defaultPersonaId` (it then returns the first declared persona), and an empty personas map (an empty overlay under the default id), and it never throws. The selection runs inside `composePrompt`, within the single `beforeModelResponse` hook. There it builds the base prompt, then the chosen persona's overlay, then the dated line. `composePrompt` also writes the chosen persona's registry `id` to `session.activePersona` on every turn, fallback included.
